applies_why: The judge marks the Isaiah 7:14 matter UNDERDETERMINED and cites that the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways, which is an ambiguity/open-verse ground governed by K-S2.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.
room: 'When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open'—I weighed whether 'word-count cuts both ways' is an impermissible open/UNDERDETERMINED treatment of ambiguous verse wording, or only evidence across verses; I read the judge as using it to keep the verse open.
why: The judge treats the Isaiah 7:14 wording as open ('word-count cuts both ways') and assigns UNDERDETERMINED, contrary to K-S2's requirement that both meanings stand and the verse not be open.
